docs.title: GitHub API Documentation
docs.text: Welcome! This is a beginner-friendly guide to understanding GitHub's API. The GitHub API allows you to access and interact with your GitHub repositories, issues, users, and more using HTTP requests.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Authentication is required to access most parts of the GitHub API. This ensures that only authorized users can read or change data.

You typically authenticate using a personal access token.

GET /user
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN
Host: api.github.com

docs.title: Issues
docs.text:
Issues are used to track bugs, features, and tasks in a repository. They are a core part of GitHub collaboration.

You can list, create, and update issues using the API.

GET /repos/OWNER/REPO/issues
Host: api.github.com

docs.title: Repositories
docs.text:
A repository (or "repo") is where your project's files live on GitHub. Repositories can be public or private.

You can use the GitHub API to create, list, update, or delete repositories.

GET /users/USERNAME/repos
Host: api.github.com

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
Users represent people using GitHub. Each user has a profile and can own repositories.

You can fetch public user data using the GitHub API.

GET /users/USERNAME
Host: api.github.com
